subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — AlphaTech billing cadence & buyer approvals
messages:

Cc: procurement@alphatech.com

Subject: AWS private offer — pricing cadence and approval flow

Hi Rachel / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and Finance asked for two specific things before we can move to a Private Offer on AWS Marketplace:

1) Pricing cadence: they want to understand whether Redwood can support quarterly invoicing vs. an annual prepay.
2) Buyer approvals: AlphaTech has a two-stage signoff — BU head + corporate procurement for any PO > $250k. We need to document the approvals path so internal systems (Coupa) can map the PO.

I've attached the RFP excerpt that lists their requirements. Can you share a concise proposal (pricing table + recommended term) that we can pass to Finance tomorrow?

Best,
Jerome
VP, Cloud Platform
AlphaTech

On Tue, Oct 19, 2026 at 09:12, Jerome Hale <jerome.hale@alphatech.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and Finance asked for two specific things before we can move to a Private Offer on AWS Marketplace:
>
> 1) Pricing cadence...

Hi Jerome / Maya —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level proposal for AlphaTech:

- Term: 12 months base with an optional 12-month auto-renew (cancelable with 60 days notice).
- Billing cadence options we can support: annual prepay, semi-annual invoicing, or quarterly invoicing (quarterly adds 1.5% processing surcharge).
- For AWS Private Offer mechanics we can (a) mark the offer as "Invoice Eligible" and (b) provide a consolidated monthly usage report for your billing system.

Attached is the internal price table (redwood_price_table_v3.xlsx) showing unit tiers and the three cadence variants. Vanessa and Vivek — can you confirm whether sales ops is comfortable with the 1.5% surcharge for quarterly billing? Also: what approval language do we need in the Private Offer to support Coupa ingestion?

Next step: I'll consolidate and send a single-page summary for Finance + Procurement by EOD.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Rachel / Vanessa —

Quick ops notes from my side:

- Quarterly invoicing is OK with FinanceOps but we need PO visibility: procurement must include the AWS Marketplace Offer ID in Coupa so our billing team can map the invoice.
- Thresholds: recommend we require corporate procurement signoff for any aggregated ARR > $250k, matching AlphaTech's ask. For POs sized between $100k-$250k, BU head signoff + email confirmation is acceptable.
- DocuSign: we'll send a DocuSign-ready PO template that includes the offer id and billing cadence field. Link to example: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/View?envelopeId=ABC-123-456

I'm attaching the sample PO template (AlphaTech_PO_Draft_v1.pdf) for legal to review.

- Action for Rachel: confirm which cadence AlphaTech prefers so we can pre-populate the invoice schedule.

Team —

Legal / contracting notes on the proposed approach:

- Term language: 12-month initial term with a one-time automatic 12-month renewal is acceptable. We should include explicit cancellation window (60 days) and a statement that renewals will maintain the then-current pricing unless otherwise agreed via amendment.
- Invoicing: we can support quarterly invoices but suggest we add a small processing fee (as Vivek recommended). Ensure the invoice schedule and payment terms (Net 30) are visible on the Private Offer landing page and mirrored on the DocuSign PO.
- Approval metadata: require a mandatory field on the PO for "Authorizing Manager (BU)" and a separate field for "Corporate Procurement Approver". That will make Coupa mapping straightforward.

I'll incorporate these edits into the PO template and push an updated DocuSign envelope. If AlphaTech requires sub-division-specific billing (multiple BU billing to separate GL codes), flag now — that adds operational complexity and may push us to annual prepay.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed Private Offer: quarterly invoicing option + approval mapping (summary)

Hi Jerome / Maya —

Per our follow-ups, please find a concise summary and ask so your Finance/Procurement can sign off:

Summary of options (choose one):
- Option A — Annual prepay (no surcharge).
- Option B — Semi-annual invoicing (0.75% surcharge).
- Option C — Quarterly invoicing (1.5% surcharge) — recommended if you need cashflow alignment.

Recommended default: Option C (quarterly) with 12-month initial term + optional 12-month renewal.

Approval mapping we will capture in the PO template:
- Field: Authorizing Manager (BU) — required.
- Field: Corporate Procurement Approver — required for POs > $250k.
- Field: AWS Marketplace Offer ID — required.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm preferred billing cadence (A/B/C) by EOD tomorrow.
2) If you need separate GL codes per BU, flag now (ops note: this will likely force annual prepay).
3) Once cadence is confirmed we will: (a) provision the Private Offer on AWS, (b) send DocuSign PO populated with your selection, and (c) route for signature.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if helpful.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
